standard.title: Compose and notate music
standard.description: compose using the elements of music and compositional devices to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning, and notate, document and/or record the music
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can manipulate elements of music and use compositional devices to communicate ideas when composing and practising music for performance (AC9AMU6C01). They can notate, document and/or record their compositions. They have not yet focused on communicating specific ideas, perspectives or meaning as a compositional intent, nor on arranging or re-imagining existing works.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students compose music using elements of music and compositional devices to communicate specific ideas, perspectives or meaning, and notate, document or record the composition in a format appropriate to the genre, style or intended performers.

nodes.label: Establishing compositional intent
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify an idea, perspective or meaning they want to communicate through music and describe how musical choices might serve that intent
nodes.minimum_width: State a compositional intent (idea, perspective, theme or purpose) and identify at least one musical element or device that could help communicate it
nodes.typical_width: Articulate a compositional intent with enough specificity to guide musical decisions; identify multiple elements or devices that could serve the intent and explain the connection
wider: Investigate how composers have used music to communicate perspectives on social issues (e.g. protest songs, nationalistic music) — analyse the musical choices made and connect them to the intended message
Compare how the same broad intent (e.g. 'friendship' or 'belonging') could be communicated differently depending on genre — what changes and what stays the same?

response_modes.reason: Students often default to vague or generic compositional intents ('I want it to sound happy') that don't drive meaningful musical decisions. Encountering a range of real compositional purposes — protest, ceremony, film scoring, community — helps students understand that intent shapes musical choices, not just mood.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The social issues direction (protest songs, nationalistic music) connects compositional intent to real-world consequences and audiences — a genuine enrichment that makes the stakes of communicating through music concrete and culturally situated.
success_criteria: States a compositional intent beyond general mood description
Identifies at least one musical element or device connected to the intent

nodes.label: Using patterns and devices as compositional material
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use harmonic, rhythmic or melodic patterns and compositional devices as the basis for a composition or improvisation
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least one pattern (e.g. ostinato, riff, chord progression) as compositional material; compose or improvise additional material over or around it
nodes.typical_width: Use multiple patterns or devices (e.g. loops, harmonic progressions, melodic motifs) in combination; make deliberate choices about how patterns are combined, varied or contrasted
wider: Create a composition built entirely from loops or layered ostinati, then compose or improvise additional melodic lines that interact with the looped material — evaluate how the layers interact
Develop an arrangement or re-imagining of an existing melody by improvising over or around given material (melody, riff or chord progression) and documenting the choices made

response_modes.reason: Students need to accumulate a working vocabulary of patterns and devices before they can combine them purposefully. Experiencing loops, ostinati, chord progressions and melodic motifs as distinct compositional tools — with their own affordances — builds the palette that compositional decision-making draws on.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The re-imagining and arrangement direction is genuinely rich — students engage with an existing musical object, make interpretive decisions about transformation, and document their reasoning. This extends well beyond minimum while staying within band.
success_criteria: Uses at least one pattern or device as compositional material
Composes or improvises additional material that relates to the pattern

nodes.label: Shaping music for purpose and context
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compose music shaped by a specific purpose or context, making decisions about form, style and instrumentation appropriate to that context
nodes.minimum_width: Compose music for a specific purpose or context (e.g. ensemble repertoire, theatrical work, event); make at least one deliberate decision about form or instrumentation based on the context
nodes.typical_width: Compose music whose form, style and instrumentation are clearly shaped by the purpose — explain how the context drove specific musical decisions
wider: Compose music for a theatrical, site-specific or media work context — consider how the non-musical context (narrative, space, visual elements) constrains and enriches the musical choices
Write a song or instrumental piece that communicates a perspective on a local issue (sustainable living, relationships, identity) — evaluate whether the musical choices support the message

response_modes.reason: Students often compose in a vacuum without considering how purpose and audience shape musical decisions. Encountering a range of real compositional contexts — fanfares, ensemble repertoire, media music, songs with social purpose — helps students understand that context is not an external constraint but a compositional driver.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The perspective/social issue direction is genuinely rich — connecting composition to real ideas and audiences makes the communicative intent of music concrete and gives students a meaningful evaluative lens beyond 'does it sound good'.
success_criteria: Composes music for an identified purpose or context
Makes at least one deliberate musical decision based on the context

nodes.label: Notating, documenting and recording
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can notate, document or record their composition in a format appropriate to the genre, style or intended performers
nodes.minimum_width: Document a composition in at least one format (staff notation, chord chart, lead sheet, percussion notation, recording, or digital file); the format is appropriate for the style
nodes.typical_width: Choose a documentation format appropriate to the genre and intended performers; explain why the chosen format suits the work better than alternatives
wider: Use software to notate or record a composition in a format appropriate to the genre — evaluate how the software shapes or constrains compositional decisions
Document an arrangement in a format appropriate for the musicians performing it, considering both their reading abilities and the conventions of the style

response_modes.reason: Students need familiarity with multiple documentation formats to make genre-appropriate choices. Encountering staff notation, chord charts, lead sheets, percussion notation and digital recording as distinct tools — each suited to different genres and performers — builds the practical literacy that appropriate documentation requires.

success_criteria: Documents the composition in at least one format
The format is appropriate for the genre or style

nodes.label: Integrated composition communicating intent
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can produce a complete composition that integrates compositional intent, use of patterns/devices, contextual shaping and appropriate documentation into a unified work
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a documented composition in which at least one musical choice can be traced back to the stated compositional intent
nodes.typical_width: Produce a documented composition in which musical choices (elements, devices, form, instrumentation) consistently serve the compositional intent; reflect on how successfully the intent is communicated
wider: Arrange a familiar piece into a different style by manipulating elements of music to convey meaning — document the arrangement in a form appropriate for the musicians performing it, explaining the interpretive choices made
Produce a composition that will be performed or shared, then evaluate audience or peer response against the intended communication — what was received as intended, what wasn't, and why?

response_modes.reason: This node is where intent, pattern use, contextual shaping and documentation come together as a single compositional act. Students discover that these are not separate steps but simultaneous considerations — a composition communicates intent through every choice, from material to documentation format.

success_criteria: At least one musical choice is traceable to the stated compositional intent
